checkOrder.law: first refusal wins; only the first is spoken — a device reading a list of charges is a system menu, not a tool
checkOrder.reason: place before lock (where you stand, then what the target is); eyes before read (the device checks the room before looking at the heart — a refused device must have done nothing in front of those witnesses, #268)

classes.trigger: the battle's witness count (#272's set) exceeds the item's ceiling

classes.dataSeat: #68's lock on the target's record — any device, any thrower
classes.source: #268's protection rule, restated as a refusal class

classes.dataSeat: ruleset flag (#109 lobby founded; #186 facilities may carry it as data)
classes.trigger: the battle's ruleset forbids the snag class

classes.instances: zero states at build — the read's honesty valve, founded before it is needed
classes.trigger: a reader-carrying device cannot complete its heart read; the device declines rather than guess (a guess is how a rescue becomes a theft by mislabel)

classes.source: capture's ordinary exclusions, restated for completeness
classes.trigger: the target is not in a throwable state (off-field, excluded condition, beyond-class frenzy); refuses ordinary throws identically

note: A refusal is the device talking, in-world, with a reason — never a system error. Its load-bearing silence (no deed, no attempt, no witness event) is what makes crowded places SAFE rather than merely crime-failing.

spoken.how: one short #23 string per class (small sets for texture), in the device's voice, naming the reason plainly; rendered through the ordinary battle text flow (#10/#23), never an error surface
spoken.test: a refusal that teaches the player nothing about the world is a failed refusal — each class's string is gameplay information (crowds are safety; this partner is protected; this place forbids it)

turnEconomy.law: a refused throw does NOT eat the action — the command returns to the ring with the turn intact; a launched throw consumes the turn (Pokemon's shape: the throw happened, the world answered)
turnEconomy.npcSide: a refused NPC device means the thrower visibly does something else with the turn (#268 symmetry) — itself readable information (#352)
turnEconomy.reason: a refusal tax would teach players never to test the device, and testing the device is how the world's rules are learned

writes.attempt: none (#348 — refusal is pre-launch by definition)
